name: Matosinhos
description: Porto's city beach. The Leixões harbour wall takes the edge off the Atlantic, which leaves gentle, forgiving waves and makes this the classroom of the north.

photo.alt: A surfer rides a small wave at Matosinhos, with the cruise terminal behind
photo.author: Bex Walton

name: Cabedelo
description: On the south bank of the Mondego river mouth, the jetty shapes one of the longest right-handers in the country. The closest good wave to Coimbra.

photo.alt: Sunset over the wet sand and the breaking waves of Cabedelo
photo.author: Telmo Pedrosa

name: Praia do Norte
description: An underwater canyon points straight at this beach and stacks winter swells into the biggest waves ever surfed. Most people watch from the lighthouse.

photo.alt: A crowd on the Nazaré lighthouse fort watches a giant wave break
photo.author: Luis Ascenso

name: Supertubos
description: Fast, hollow and heavy over a shallow sandbank. The world tour stops here every year, and the name tells you what everyone comes for.

photo.alt: A professional surfer launches off the lip of a wave at Supertubos
photo.author: Luis Ascenso

name: Ribeira d'Ilhas
description: A long right-hander peeling over flat reef, at the heart of Europe's first World Surfing Reserve. Consistent all year and rarely empty.

photo.alt: Lines of swell wrap around the reef at Ribeira d'Ilhas, seen from the cliff
photo.author: Adamina

name: Carcavelos
description: Lisbon's home break, a short train ride from the city. It faces south, so the prevailing north wind blows offshore and grooms the winter swells.

photo.alt: Surfers on a breaking wave at Carcavelos under a pastel sunset sky
photo.author: Sonse

name: Arrifana
description: A crescent bay tucked under the cliffs of the Costa Vicentina. Mellow waves on the sand, and a serious right-hander off the point when a big swell arrives.

photo.alt: The bay of Arrifana and its headland at dusk
photo.author: Geerd-Olaf Freyer

name: Tonel
description: Beside the fortress of Sagres, at the south-western tip of Europe. Open to every westerly swell, so there is a wave here when the south coast is flat.

photo.alt: Foam runs up the sand at Tonel beach, below the orange cliffs of Sagres
photo.author: dronepicr
